item.title: Precios de bonos del Tesoro de EEUU caen mientras inversores esperan datos de inflación
item.description: Los precios de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos cayeron el viernes, revirtiendo parte de las ganancias de inicios de semana, mientras el valor del petróleo se mantenía alto y los inversores aguardaban los próximos informes de inflación en busca de pistas sobre las medidas que tomará la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
item.content:encoded: Los precios de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos cayeron el viernes, revirtiendo parte de las ganancias de inicios de semana, mientras el valor del petróleo se mantenía alto y los inversores aguardaban los próximos informes de inflación en busca de pistas sobre las medidas que tomará la Reserva Federal. El rendimiento de referencia a 10 años avanzó 2,8 puntos básicos, al 5,261%, tras alcanzar esta semana un máximo en 24 años. Sin embargo, en la semana, los rendimientos a 10 años bajaron un 3,5 puntos básicos, su mayor descenso semanal en dos meses. El retorno a 30 años subió levemente, al 5,608%, pero cayó 2,9 puntos básicos en términos semanales. Cuando los precios de los bonos del Tesoro caen, los rendimientos suben. En el extremo más corto de la curva, la rentabilidad a dos años , que suele reflejar las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés, subió 4,4 puntos básicos, al 4,799%. La curva de rendimientos se aplanaba por segundo día consecutivo el viernes, y el diferencial entre los rendimientos a dos y 10 años se redujo de 46,7 a 45,5 puntos básicos. Los agentes en el mercado tienen la mirada puesta en los datos de inflación de la próxima semana. Los próximos informes del Índice de Precios al Consumidor y del Índice de Precios al Productor se publicarán el miércoles y el jueves, respectivamente. Ruchir Sharma, economista de Nomura, escribió en una nota de investigación que es probable que la inflación subyacente del IPC se haya desacelerado en septiembre a medida que se desvaneció el impulso temporal a los precios de las telecomunicaciones inalámbricas. "Teniendo en cuenta la poca urgencia de realizar aumentos de tasas consecutivas, así como la proximidad de las elecciones de mitad de mandato, es improbable que nuestro pronóstico de inflación aumente la probabilidad de un alza de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal en octubre", dijo Sharma.

item.title: Mike Ditka, Hall of Fame player and Bears coach, dies at 86
item.description: Mike Ditka, a Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end best known as the slick-haired and mustachioed head coach who led the NFL's Chicago Bears to their only Super Bowl triumph in 1986, has died. He was 86.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mike Ditka, a Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end best known as the slick-haired and mustachioed head coach who led the NFL's Chicago Bears to their only Super Bowl triumph in 1986, has died. He was 86. Ditka's death was announced in a statement by his family on Friday. No cause of death was given. "It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend," Ditka's family said in a statement. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. "Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever." Revered in Chicago and famous nationwide as "Da Coach," Ditka was a blunt, straight-talking legend with a devoted following and restaurants bearing his name. He also sold a number of products with his name on, including cigars, sausages and wine. TRANSFORMED THE TIGHT END POSITION As a player, Ditka revolutionized the tight end position and was a five-time Pro Bowl selection while playing with the Bears from 1961-66 before moving on to the Philadelphia Eagles and then the Dallas Cowboys, where he featured in the team's Super Bowl triumph in January 1972. Selected fifth overall by the Bears in the 1961 NFL Draft, Ditka introduced a new dimension to the tight end position that once was viewed primarily as an assignment for a tough, talented blocker. While Ditka, also affectionately known as "Iron Mike," was a superior blocker, he became one of the first tight ends to catch a large number of passes. He earned Rookie of the Year honors after becoming the first tight end in NFL history to record 1,000 receiving yards in a season and went on to win the 1963 NFL championship with Chicago prior to the start of the Super Bowl era. At the time of his retirement after the 1972 season, Ditka ranked second among all tight ends in receptions, according to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He is also the only individual in the NFL's modern era to win a league title with the same team as a player and head coach. "Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach and proud icon and ambassador for our organization is immeasurable," the team said in a statement. "His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations." DITKA 'EPITOMIZED FOOTBALL' Following his playing career Ditka became a member of Tom Landry's coaching staff in Dallas where he won a Super Bowl. He eventually returned to Chicago as head coach and turned the Bears into one of the league's most dominant champions. The Bears team that Ditka led to Super Bowl glory featured one of the most vaunted defenses in NFL history and a top-ranked offense. With the likes of Walter Payton, William "The Refrigerator" Perry, Jim McMahon and Mike Singletary, the Bears transcended professional sports and became a global pop culture phenomenon after recording “The Super Bowl Shuffle” rap song and accompanying music video that became an unlikely hit. The song was released weeks before the Bears beat the New England Patriots 46-10 in the Super Bowl. At the time, it was the largest margin of victory in any Super Bowl. After the game, the Chicago players carried Ditka, who was wearing a sleeveless Bears sweater over a formal dress shirt and tie, off the field on their shoulders. "Mike Ditka epitomized football over so many years. He brought intensity, authenticity and an unmistakable personality to everything he did," NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "As a Hall of Fame player, Super Bowl-winning coach with his beloved and iconic Bears, and as a broadcaster, Mike served as an ambassador for the game and inspired generations of fans."

item.title: UAE says Omani flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack on Tel Aviv flight
item.description: UAE public prosecutors say the plan was inspired by 9/11 attacks on the US. The suspect had used two previous flights to Tel Aviv to familiarize himself with the flight route and the airport.
item.dc:creator: Yasmine Ghania, Enas Alashray, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: An Omani flydubai co-pilot had intended to [USN:L1N45M07P TEXT:"seize a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight"] and crash it into a terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport on September 30 in a suicide attack before he was thwarted by the captain, the UAE attorney general said on Friday. Attorney General Hamad Saif al Shamsi's statement did not appear to implicate flydubai in any wrongdoing, and contained the most detailed account yet from prosecutors about what they believe to have happened. Flydubai was not immediately available for comment. The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors think, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1. It found the suspect had used two previous flights to Tel Aviv to "familiarise himself with the flight route and the airport", the state news agency WAM reported. It is the first public confirmation of the co-pilot's 9/11 inspiration. The aircraft was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies. The incident caused the airliner to [USN:L4N45Q00M TEXT:"plunge"] 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect was transferred to the UAE, flydubai's home country. SUSPECT MET PROFESSIONAL AND SECURITY REQUIREMENTS Investigators examined flydubai's recruiting procedures and found the suspect had met all professional and security requirements, including holding a pilot's licence and providing a certificate of good conduct. "However, none of the procedures revealed any indications of his extremist views or his intention to carry out a terrorist plot," Al Shamsi added. He said the 29-year-old had worked for airlines in different countries including Oman Air before joining flydubai in January 2026. The investigation found there were signs of the suspect drifting towards "extremism and terrorism" as early as 2017, while he was studying in Australia. Royal Air Maroc has said that he underwent three months of training there in 2025, but that his application to work for the airline afterwards was rejected. UAE officials have not identified the suspect; however, a person with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters he had been identified as [USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"Hammam al-Hammami"], an Omani national. Al Shamsi said the suspect had told investigators he had prepared psychologically and physically for the attack by viewing material promoting terrorism and taking boxing lessons. Saudi Arabia has launched a [USN:L1N45S12C TEXT:"separate safety investigation"] into flight FZ1073, sources told Reuters.

item.title: Vance says he won't watch livestream of execution; Trump remains silent
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance said on Friday that he would not watch a livestream of the military execution of the gunman who killed 13 people at Fort Hood military base in 2009, while President Donald Trump has yet to comment on the Pentagon plan.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: US Vice President JD Vance said on Friday that he would not watch a livestream of the military execution of the gunman who killed 13 people at Fort Hood military base in 2009, while President Donald Trump has yet to comment on the Pentagon plan. "I don't know that that's actually going to happen," Vance told reporters while campaigning in Ohio. "If it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it." Trump said at a White House event on Friday that former Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan would be executed by firing squad. But he has not commented on the livestream plan announced by Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on Thursday that has drawn [USN:FWN45V0WT TEXT:"criticism at home and abroad"]. Some Republican lawmakers and conservative strategists have criticized the decision. Republican US Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina called the idea "beyond disgusting" in a social media post. "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," said the senator, a frequent Trump critic who is not running for reelection. "It should not be happening in America." Hasan is set to become the first person to be executed by US military firing squad since 1945. The execution is scheduled for December 3 at the same sprawling Texas base where Hasan opened fire with a handgun in a medical facility.

item.title: Trump says Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Timothy Gardner, Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine. Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, are near a record and risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress. Diesel prices fell after the announcement, but analysts said the deal may not be enough to keep them down. Trump said on social media he had a "highly successful" discussion with President Vladimir Putin in which they agreed that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to US and global markets, equal to about 2.25 million barrels of fuel. The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day. After the call, an envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, praised cooperation between Russia and the US in a post on X. Dmitriev asked US officials during his visit to Washington last month for licenses to export diesel to the US market to be granted to all Russian major oil firms, sources familiar with the situation said. In October 2025, the US imposed sanctions on Russian oil companies over Moscow's war that began in 2022. The diesel exports could provide Moscow with billions of dollars in revenues that could help Putin continue the war with Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy criticized the deal, announced while a Ukrainian delegation was in the US to discuss how to seek a resolution of the war, as a "weak decision on the part of strong partners." "Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy," he said on X. The deal was also criticized by US lawmakers including Trump's fellow Republican, Representative Don Bacon, who said it is time to apply more sanctions that [USN:L1N4431OK TEXT:"Congress passed recently"], not lift the measures. "Now is the time to use those sanctions to squeeze Putin’s war machine, not reward a dictator by putting more money in his hands while he continues targeting and killing Ukrainian civilians," Bacon said on X. The US Treasury Department issued a license allowing importation of Russian diesel until April 7. Trump said Russia would supply another 500,000 tons in November and a further 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." Even more would follow, Trump said, "based on the condition of their diesel refineries," which have been damaged by Ukrainian attacks. 'NOTHING BURGER' Analysts said the agreement was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices. "I cannot overstate how much of a nothing burger this is," Rory Johnston, an oil market researcher and founder of CommodityContext.com, said on X, adding that Russia usually exports much more diesel than volumes in the deal when its refinery fleet is not under attack. "It's clearly not a fix, but another stream to aid a very tight diesel market," said Jim Mitchell, an analyst at consultancy Wood Mackenzie. [USN:L1N45U0FQ TEXT:"Diesel prices"], which are often a big driver of inflation, are up 70% since the US and Israel launched the war with Iran on February 28. The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered a severe global fuel supply crunch, pushing average US diesel prices to $6.28 a gallon on Thursday, according to the AAA motorist group. Prices have stayed high despite two recent moves by Trump to boost supplies of the fuel: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is normally used for farm equipment. US diesel futures fell almost 5% following news of the deal and were trading at $4.64 a gallon. "Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump said. DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT Three industry sources said earlier on Friday that Trump will issue a directive in the coming days to some US department heads to find ways to control diesel prices. The directive, which they said could take the form of a presidential memo, will push officials to find ways to bypass local and state regulations blocking energy production and use the Cold War-era Defense Production Act to increase output of oil and fuel. Under the DPA, the president can authorize US-backed loans or loan guarantees to expand domestic manufacturing of critical materials and to require companies to prioritize government contracts for essential goods. The White House has been weighing how to use the DPA to expand refining capacity as the war with Iran exposes US vulnerability to supply disruptions and price spikes. Refining executives [USN:L1N45214P TEXT:"told administration officials"] last month that federal money would be better directed toward making refineries more efficient or expanding plants rather than financing a new refinery, which would be more costly and take years to complete.

item.title: Peso mexicano amplía baja tras Banxico; real sube tras sondeos electorales
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaron mixtas el viernes en una jornada de oscilaciones del dólar y de los precios del crudo, con las divisas de las principales economías de la región en sentidos opuestos, ya que el peso mexicano se hundió y el real brasileño avanzó.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaron mixtas el viernes en una jornada de oscilaciones del dólar y de los precios del crudo, con las divisas de las principales economías de la región en sentidos opuestos, ya que el peso mexicano se hundió y el real brasileño avanzó. * A nivel global, el índice dólar repuntó tras un descenso de más temprano y marcó su cuarta alza semanal consecutiva, su racha más larga desde mayo de 2025; mientras que los precios del crudo cambiaron de tendencia y avanzaron ante la llegada del huracán Isaías, lo que provocaba cierres de producción en aguas estadounidenses. * En ese contexto, el peso mexicano se hundía cerca del cierre un 1,26%, a 18,4072 unidades por dólar, ampliando las fuertes pérdidas de la víspera, luego de que las minutas de la última reunión del Banco de México mostraron que tres miembros de su Junta de Gobierno señalaron que podrían considerarse futuros recortes en la tasa de interés en caso de mejorar las perspectivas inflacionarias. * Eso planteaba temores en los inversionistas por una posible ampliación de diferenciales con la tasa de interés de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos. Los mercados esperan que la Fed aumente el costo del crédito en diciembre. El peso marcó su quinta semana de pérdidas. * "En 2026 el peso mexicano acumula una depreciación frente al dólar de 2,37% (...) y hoy el tipo de cambio tocó un máximo de 18,4985 pesos por dólar, no visto desde el 25 de noviembre del 2025. Desde el mínimo en el año de 16,8573 pesos por dólar registrado el 4 de septiembre, el peso acumula una depreciación de 9,36%", dijo Banco Base en un reporte. * La entidad dijo que la debilidad del peso mexicano en las últimas semanas se ha visto fomentada por la señal de recortes adicionales en la tasa de interés por parte de Banco de México; menos atractivo de operaciones por carry trade; el fortalecimiento del dólar a nivel global y una mayor percepción de riesgo sobre México. * Mientras, el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, escaló un 1,63%, a 66.048,57 puntos. * En Brasil el real ganó un 0,76% a 4,9856 por dólar, para escalar un más de un 4% en la semana. El referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) trepó un 1,33%, a 209.017 puntos, según datos preliminares de cierre, para marcar un máximo histórico y también intradía. * Los mercados fueron apuntalados por recientes sondeos electorales de cara a la segunda vuelta entre el presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y el senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro. * Los sondeos de Datafolha y de Atlas/Bloomberg daban como ganador del balotaje al senador Bolsonaro, quien venció en la primera vuelta, pese a que las encuestas apuntaban a una ventaja de Lula. Los mercados esperan que Bolsonaro aplique un mayor control sobre las cuentas fiscales del país. * El peso chileno , cerró con un retroceso del 0,27%, en 981,90/982,20 unidades por dólar, pero acumuló un avance semanal del 1,05%. Por su parte, el principal índice de la bolsa de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , clausuró la sesión con un alza del 0,17%, en 11.043,36 puntos. * El peso colombiano subió un 0,87%, a 3.189 unidades por dólar, y en la bolsa el índice accionario COLCAP (.COLCAP) ganó un 0,21%, a 2.531,15 puntos. * El peso argentino mayorista cerró estable a estable en 1.517 unidades por dólar para la venta. Desde el banco central (BCRA), entidad que regula la liquidez del mercado, se compró 69 millones de dólares el viernes y se acerca a acumular adquisiciones por 15.000 millones de dólares en lo que va del año. * "El BCRA mantuvo el ritmo de compras significativo que viene caracterizando a octubre", dijo Portfolio Personal Inversiones (PPI). * El índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires, en tanto, retrocedió un 0,16%. * La moneda peruana, el sol , finalizó con una leve baja del 0,03%, a 3,4430/3,4460 unidades por dólar, mientras que en la semana se depreció un 0,29%. item.title: Plaza financiera argentina opera sin rumbo definido
item.description: Los mercados financieros de Argentina operaron dispares el viernes debido a la cautela de los inversores institucionales antes del feriado por la celebración del 'Día del Respeto a la Diversidad Cultural'.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los mercados financieros de Argentina operaron dispares el viernes debido a la cautela de los inversores institucionales antes del feriado por la celebración del [USN:L1N45V0G6 TEXT:"'Día del Respeto a la Diversidad Cultural'"]. Pese a la prudencia que se evidencia en el ámbito local, los operadores mantienen su atención en el contexto externo, principalmente en el precio internacional del crudo y el conflicto en Oriente Medio. El valor del petróleo "retrocede después de que (el presidente Donald) Trump afirmara que Estados Unidos no atacará a Irán antes de las elecciones de medio término de noviembre. Además, mencionó que hubo 'conversaciones productivas' con Teherán", expresó Quantum Finanzas. El índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires retrocedió un 0,16% al cierre, mientras que los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil mejoraron un 0,2% promedio, durante una semana con viento en popa por el triunfo electoral de la derecha en Brasil. Por su parte, el riesgo país se ubicaba en 590 puntos básicos (2000 GMT), luego de anotar un nivel de 655 unidades al cierre de la semana previa, con un peso argentino mayorista estable a 1.517 por dólar para la venta. Desde el banco central (BCRA), entidad que regula la liquidez del mercado, se compró 69 millones de dólares este viernes y se acerca a acumular adquisiciones por 15.000 millones de dólares en lo que va del año. "El BCRA mantuvo el ritmo de compras significativo que viene caracterizando a octubre" afirmó Portfolio Personal Inversiones (PPI). Operadores prevén que el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de septiembre registre una leve aceleración en relación al 1,7% anotado el mes previo. Un sondeo de Reuters estimó que el IPC podría registrar una variación de [USN:L1N45U0LZ TEXT:"1,9% en el noveno mes del año"]. "El IPC de CABA (Ciudad de Buenos Aires) registró una variación de 1,8% mensual en septiembre, frente al 1,7% de agosto, interrumpiendo la desaceleración de los meses previos, aunque manteniéndose por debajo del 2%", añadió Quantum Finanzas. El Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) dará a conocer el dato oficial del IPC de septiembre el martes por la tarde. Por otra parte, un reciente informe de la consultora Qualy sobre indicadores adelantados de la actividad estima que se amplia la brecha de la economía a "dos velocidades". "El escenario de 'dos velocidades' se profundiza, marcado por el contraste entre la solidez de los sectores extractivos y exportadores frente a la fragilidad del mercado interno", según Qualy. "El segmento energético se consolida como el principal motor de la economía gracias al extraordinario desempeño de Vaca Muerta", mientras que "las actividades dependientes del consumo masivo y la inversión privada enfrentan un terreno de contracción y elevada capacidad ociosa", añadió.

item.title: How the US plan to livestream an execution compares with global practice
item.description: The U.S. military plans to livestream the Dec. 3 execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. military plans to livestream the Dec. 3 execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting. If carried out as planned, death penalty experts said it would mark the first known broadcast or livestream of a lawful execution. Executions are generally conducted behind prison walls, and internet platforms and governments have spent years trying to limit the circulation of violent execution footage. HAS A LAWFUL EXECUTION EVER BEEN LIVESTREAMED OR BROADCAST TO THE PUBLIC BEFORE? Death penalty experts consulted by Reuters said they were unaware of any previous lawful execution that had been livestreamed or broadcast to a public audience. Execution footage has occasionally emerged after the event. The hanging of former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein in 2006, for example, was seen around the world after official and unofficial recordings circulated online and through broadcasters, though it was not shown live. Broadcasts and livestreams today are common for court proceedings, parliamentary debates and other state functions, but not for judicial executions. HOW UNUSUAL IS THIS COMPARED WITH MODERN EXECUTION PRACTICES AROUND THE WORLD? Public executions have become rare worldwide, with most countries that retain the death penalty carrying out executions away from public view. According to Amnesty International, public executions recorded in recent years have largely been concentrated in Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan. The execution would also be notable in the United States. Public executions largely disappeared during the 20th century, and death penalty experts cited by Reuters said the last legally sanctioned public execution took place in 1936. Hasan's execution would be the first carried out by firing squad by the U.S. military since the 1945 execution of Eddie Slovik, who was convicted of desertion during World War Two. HOW HAS THE INTERNET CHANGED THE CIRCULATION OF EXECUTION FOOTAGE? The internet has transformed execution imagery from a local event into content capable of reaching global audiences within minutes. Militant groups such as Islamic State became notorious for producing professionally edited execution videos that were distributed online as propaganda and recruitment tools. Criminal organisations, including Mexican drug cartels, have also circulated violent footage to intimidate rivals and project power. The ability of users to rapidly copy, repost and redistribute content has made it more difficult for governments and technology companies to control the spread of such material. WHAT HAS BEEN THE REACTION FROM GOVERNMENTS AND TECH COMPANIES? Governments and technology companies have generally moved in the opposite direction, attempting to reduce rather than expand access to graphic execution footage. Major social media platforms have spent years removing execution videos linked to extremist organisations and other violent groups. One of the first public governmental reactions came from New Zealand, whose chief censor said authorities would have little practical ability to prevent residents from accessing a livestream while it was taking place. Livestreams pose particular challenges for platforms because footage can be viewed, copied and redistributed before moderation systems can intervene. Even countries that still conduct public executions have often restricted filming and broadcast rights. Saudi Arabia historically carried out public executions before spectators, but recording them was prohibited and such public executions had largely ceased by 2019. (This story has been corrected to fix the year to 2001, not 2021, in paragraph 15.)

item.title: US immigration chiefs defend shooting of New York man, attack 'sanctuary' policies
item.description: US immigration officials defended federal agents on Friday who shot and wounded a New York City man in his car with a young child believed to be his son in the back seat and rebuked Mayor Zohran Mamdani for his condemnation of immigration agents.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Allen, Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: US immigration officials defended federal agents on Friday who shot and wounded a New York City man in his car with a young child believed to be his son in the back seat and rebuked Mayor Zohran Mamdani for his condemnation of immigration agents. US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said at a press conference that officers did not know the child was in the car at the time they opened fire and accused the man, a Dominican who was the target of the operation, of endangering both officers and the child. The man, identified by officials as Oscar Belgal, refused to exit his car when approached by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers on Thursday afternoon in Marble Hill, Manhattan's northernmost neighborhood. Before Belgal, federal immigration officers had shot at least 21 people, killing 7 of them, across the US since President Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025 promising record-breaking deportations, an unusually high number for civil law enforcement operations. Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, said at the press conference that Belgal accelerated his car and struck two ICE vehicles and appeared to be "going towards officers" when they began shooting. In other violent incidents, initial accounts from ICE or the Department of Homeland Security have repeatedly been contradicted by video and other evidence, sometimes in court, and Reuters was unable to verify Charles' account. Belgal suffered a superficial wound to his neck, Charles said. He is being held in a detention facility outside New York state. Belgal's 5-year-old son was in the back seat at the time, according to police. Belgal can be seen sitting by a car with his hands cuffed behind him and patches of what appear to be fresh blood on the tarmac in a three-minute body-worn camera video released by the New York Police Department on Friday, with several agents dressed in plain clothes standing around him. One is holding a rifle and wearing a fluorescent reflective vest. A crowd of angry onlookers gathered outside a corner store shouts at the agents from the sidewalk. Several city police officers pick up Belgal by his arms and legs, put him in their car and take him to a hospital. "Yo, put pressure, put pressure!" one of the police officers instructs his colleagues with Belgal in the back of the police car. Mullin said body-worn camera video from ICE agents would also be released. Belgal is a Dominican who is in the country illegally and had previously evaded an effort by ICE agents to apprehend him in September, according to US officials. He pleaded guilty last year to fourth-degree grand larceny for stealing something from another person, leading to a sentence of five years on probation, and is due in court in December on charges of criminal sale of a controlled substance, to which he pleaded not guilty, according to New York court records. Speaking to reporters late on Thursday at the scene of the shooting, Mamdani, noting he himself was an immigrant, condemned ICE as "rotten to the core" and said he had tried unsuccessfully to secure Belgal's release in phone calls with Trump and Mullin. Mamdani said the shooting is "further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity, that they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbors than they could ever have claimed to save." In response on Friday, Mullin attacked Mamdani and criticized New York's "sanctuary" policies, which restrict how much city agencies and police cooperate with immigration authorities unless a person has been convicted of violent or otherwise serious felonies. Trump says aggressive efforts to deport immigrants are necessary to protect the safety of native-born Americans. Public defenders at agencies that have represented Belgal in court also condemned the shooting. Legal Aid said in a statement the shooting amounted to "an urgent call to rein in ICE's use of force and hold federal immigration agents accountable," calling on city prosecutors to investigate the agents involved.

item.title: US imposes sanctions on ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: The Trump administration has long been hostile to the court and has previously imposed sanctions on its prosecutors and judges.
item.dc:creator: Humeyra Pamuk, Steve Holland, Anthony Deutsch
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump's administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court on Friday, hours after one of its [USN:L8N45V0JG TEXT:"former judges won the Nobel Peace Prize"], putting Washington on a diplomatic collision course with European allies. The court denounced the move as an "assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order," and called on its 125 member states to take action to defend it. "The Court cannot stand alone. Its fate now rests also in the hands of the states that created it," it said in a statement. "This is not just about defending a single institution, but about safeguarding the international order grounded upon the rule of law. History will judge this moment." The Trump administration has long been hostile to the court, founded in 2002 [USN:L6N3VQ0DE TEXT:"to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide"], and has previously [USN:O8N42O02H TEXT:"imposed sanctions on its prosecutors and judges"]. Friday's move goes much further, potentially punishing companies that provide services to the court itself, amounting to an unprecedented attack on an institution founded on an international treaty. The US initially signed the Rome Statute that founded the court but never ratified it. "President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement, first published by Reuters. "That is why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate." SANCTIONS INCLUDE GRACE PERIOD The US Treasury announced the sanctions with a six-month initial grace period, and some other exemptions that would allow some transactions for telecoms, software, payment of pensions and transactions related to detainees. Rubio said the sanctions had been structured to give the court and its member states an opportunity to address US concerns, and would be adjusted if those demands were not met. Washington has denounced the ICC over arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and an investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, which the ICC says is "deprioritized." Rubio in his statement cited calls from outside experts for the ICC to prosecute American service members, border patrol agents and elected leaders. ICC officials have not taken steps toward such prosecutions. "The sanctions are intended to undermine the rule of law internationally and the work that an independent judicial institution is doing," ICC Deputy Prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan told Reuters. "Our work will continue across all our situations, our investigations and our prosecutions." EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on social media that the six-month period "offers a window for dialogue" but added that the bloc "has options to ensure that (the ICC) can continue its vital work." Belgium's foreign minister called for an EU blocking statute to be activated to protect the court. The ICC has issued arrest warrants against more than 70 people, including world leaders and major figures in global conflicts. In addition to Netanyahu, it has sought the arrest of Hamas figures. Others who were the subject of arrest warrants include Russian President Vladimir Putin, former Sudan President Omar al-Bashir and former Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi. Charges against Kenyan President William Ruto and former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta were withdrawn. NOBEL COMMITTEE CITES POLITICAL ATTACKS IN AWARDING PRIZE Despite [USN:L6N45G1AB TEXT:"US calls for countries to quit the court"], it has received strong backing from most member states, which include all EU countries and all members of the NATO alliance apart from the United States and Turkey. It is based in the Netherlands, an EU and NATO member. The Nobel Prize awarded hours earlier to South African jurist Navi Pillay, who sat on the ICC's Appeals Chamber from 2003-2008, was explicitly described by the prize committee as a gesture of support for such tribunals at a time when "judges and institutions of international law are under political attack". "An international legal system in which war criminals are held to account and the victims of abuse see justice served is a precondition for a peaceful world," the prize committee said. US sanctions typically bar all US-based companies from any work with a sanctioned organization, forcing banks to shut accounts, insurers to end coverage and software companies to halt cooperation. The Trump administration previously imposed targeted sanctions on court officials during his first term, which were rescinded under President Joe Biden. Washington announced new sanctions just days after Trump returned to office in January 2025. Court officials have been preparing for months for the prospect of [USN:L6N45D0HW TEXT:"sanctions on the court"] itself, shifting office computers from Microsoft software to open-source equivalents and making new arrangements for banking and health insurance.

item.title: Crudo cierra al alza por interrupciones de la producción debido a huracán
item.description: Los precios del petróleo cerraron al alza el viernes, mientras el huracán Isaías avanzaba hacia el norte del golfo de México y las petroleras paralizaban más del 70% de la producción de crudo en aguas estadounidenses.
item.dc:creator: Erwin Seba
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo cerraron al alza el viernes, mientras el huracán Isaías avanzaba hacia el norte del golfo de México y las petroleras paralizaban más del 70% de la producción de crudo en aguas estadounidenses. A primera hora de la sesión, los precios del crudo habían bajado, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo que las conversaciones con Irán para poner fin a la guerra en Oriente Medio habían sido "productivas". Los futuros del crudo Brent cerraron en 104,72 dólares, con un alza 44 centavos, o un 0,42%, mientras que los del West Texas Intermediate de Estados Unidos cerraron en 91,85 dólares el barril, con una subida de 36 centavos, o un 0,39%. Los planes de China, el principal importador mundial de petróleo, de reanudar las exportaciones de combustible refinado tras una breve interrupción durante las vacaciones de la "Semana Dorada", también habían presionado los precios. En términos semanales, tanto el Brent como el WTI acumulaban alzas. La promesa de Trump sobre Irán, junto con la reanudación de las exportaciones de productos por parte de China, estaban provocando una caída de los precios, dijo Tamas Varga, analista de PVM Oil Associates. Los precios han mostrado volatilidad esta semana debido al aumento de las amenazas al tráfico marítimo en el golfo Pérsico y el estrecho de Ormuz, por donde antes de la guerra circulaban cargamentos equivalentes a alrededor del 20% del petróleo y los combustibles mundiales. La guerra de Irán y el conflicto entre Rusia y Ucrania han interrumpido el suministro de combustibles refinados como la gasolina, el combustible para aviones y, especialmente, el diésel. El mercado petrolero también se enfrenta al huracán Isaías en el golfo de México, donde los productores han suspendido la producción de unos 1,3 millones de barriles al día, lo que supone el 62,9% de la producción actual de petróleo hasta el jueves, según autoridades.

item.title: Qualcomm and Arm jury to return next week after deliberations in contract dispute case
item.description: The jury in a lawsuit by chipmaker Qualcomm against chip technology supplier Arm Holdings did not reach a verdict on Friday as to whether Arm breached licensing agreements and intentionally sabotaged some of Qualcomm's dealings with Meta Platforms .
item.dc:creator: Tom Hals, Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: The jury in a [USN:L6N45R04D TEXT:"lawsuit by chipmaker"] Qualcomm (QCOM.O) against chip technology supplier Arm Holdings (O9Ty.F) did not reach a verdict on Friday as to whether Arm breached licensing agreements and intentionally sabotaged some of Qualcomm's dealings with Meta Platforms (META.O) . The five-day trial that wrapped up this week was the second in two years between the companies, highlighting the deterioration of their business relationship after SoftBank Group (9984.T) acquired control of Arm in 2016 and Arm shifted from licensing the technology needed to make chips to selling chips of its own. At stake is whether Qualcomm, whose license for Arm's computing architecture runs until 2033, can eventually agree to terms for new versions of Arm's architecture. After deliberating for about four hours Friday, the jury had not reached a verdict, indicating it would return to deliberations on Tuesday. Qualcomm wants the jury to find that Arm breached its licensing agreements by withholding software patches and tools for its designs and by violating an agreement that was meant to ensure Qualcomm paid within 10% of the lowest price for Arm's processor designs. It also wants the jury to find that Arm tried to torpedo Qualcomm's dealings with Meta by leaking to Bloomberg an Arm letter in 2024 notifying Qualcomm it was allegedly in breach of a key license agreement. Arm's legal team this week tried to focus the jury on its claim that Qualcomm had not suffered any harm from the allegations in its lawsuit, which Arm cast as an attempt to exert leverage as the two fought over licensing terms. A related bench trial also took place this week over whether Arm is negotiating in good faith over those terms, though a decision on that could come well after Friday's verdict. The trial in Wilmington, Delaware, federal court hinged on many of the same episodes as the 2024 trial in which Arm failed to convince a jury that Qualcomm had breached its licensing agreement with Arm. Both trials included testimony by both Arm CEO Rene Haas and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon and were overseen by US District Judge Maryellen Noreika. Qualcomm's lawyer Karen Dunn said in her opening statement that the case was very serious for the company. "It’s really bad because Qualcomm’s entire chip business depends on Arm and on Arm honoring its contract and honoring its promises," she said on Monday. Qualcomm wanted Noreika to rule prior to trial that a clause in the licensing agreements meant that Qualcomm could stop paying royalties for five years if the contract were breached. She has not issued her ruling, and Arm has argued the royalty penalty is unenforceable. "They were not harmed in the least," Arm's attorney Gregg LoCascio told the jury on Monday.

item.title: Wall Street posts weekly gains with earnings, inflation data on tap
item.description: Wall Street ended higher on Friday as investors shifted their focus to next week, with third-quarter earnings season set to start and inflation data expected, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's next policy decision.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ended higher on Friday as investors shifted their focus to next week, with third-quarter earnings season set to start and inflation data expected, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's next policy decision. All three major US stock indexes advanced on the day, logging weekly gains. The small-cap Russell 2000 (.RUT) , however, ended lower than last Friday's close. "It's the kind of back-and-forth market we've been in where we have the reversal of sentiment around Iran," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky. "With conflicting headlines coming out of the White House and parties in the Middle East, there's just no edge there." "That's why it's a fairly tepid rally," Mayfield added. [USN:L1N45V03A TEXT:"Crude prices"] initially retreated after President Donald Trump said the US will not launch any attacks on Iran before the midterm elections, adding that talks between Washington and Tehran aimed at ending the market-rattling Iran war were "productive." Front-month West Texas Intermediate oil and Brent crude both settled up 0.4%. [USN:L1N45V0H5 TEXT:"Benchmark Treasury yields"] edged higher, but remained below Wednesday's 24-year high. BANKS DUE TO REPORT EARNINGS Third-quarter reporting season begins in earnest next week, with big US banks Wells Fargo (WFC.N) , Goldman Sachs (GS.N) , Citigroup (C.N) , JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) , Bank of America (BAC.N) and Morgan Stanley (MS.N) scheduled to release results. Analysts estimate S&P 500 annual earnings growth of 30.6%, on aggregate, for the July-September period, with energy and technology posting the largest year-on-year earnings growth of 123% and 66.5%, respectively, according to LSEG data. The mood of American consumers, who shoulder about 70% of the US economy, has soured this month, according to the University of Michigan, with near-term expectations deteriorating to an all-time low. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 423.31 points, or 0.83%, to 51,654.95, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 46.15 points, or 0.59%, to 7,811.51 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 172.83 points, or 0.64%, to 27,366.17. Among the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, communication services (.SPLRCL) was the lone percentage loser. AI-related momentum stocks were generally higher, with the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF up 1% as the US bull market, largely driven by the AI boom, approaches its [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"four-year anniversary"]. "Chips have been this year's story," said Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs in Dallas. "(It's) a multidecade technological change and just at the beginning of whatever's happening, not at the end." Elon Musk's [USN:L6N45U1AK TEXT:"SpaceX"] (SPCX.O) struck a deal to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio, posing a direct challenge to US wireless companies. Telecom firms T-Mobile US (TMUS.O) , AT&T (T.N) , and Verizon (VZ.N) dropped between 8.8% and 13.3%. [USN:L4N45V0SK TEXT:"Humana"] (HUM.N) jumped 11.6% after US government data showed 95% of the health insurer's members were in Medicare Advantage plans rated four stars or higher for 2027. [USN:L6N45V0A6 TEXT:"Apple"] (AAPL.O) slid 1.1% after a media report that the iPhone maker has told some suppliers to cut production of components for its newly launched iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, as soaring memory chip costs and price increases dampen consumer demand. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.65-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 141 new highs and 183 new lows on the NYSE.
